problems.title: I click a button that updates state, but logging it right after still shows the old value
problems.body: I have a button that calls setCount(count + 1). If I console.log(count) on the very next line, it still prints the old number, even though the screen updates correctly a moment later. Why does the log look wrong?

problems.title: I get a 'Not Found' page for a route I just added in Flask
problems.body: I added a new @app.route('/hello') to my Flask app, but opening it in the browser shows a 404 error. My other routes all work fine.

problems.title: git push keeps saying 'failed to push some refs'
problems.body: Every time I try to push my branch I get this rejection. I already ran git pull before pushing, but it still happens.

problems.title: My Python function runs fine but prints None instead of the number I expected
problems.body: I wrote a function that works out a total inside itself, but when I print the result of calling it, I get None instead of the number.

answers.body: That's normal — React doesn't update state instantly, so logging right after setCount() still shows the old value. The screen is correct because React re-renders on the next cycle. If you want to see the updated value, put your console.log inside a useEffect that watches count instead.

Adding on to the above — if you need the new value for something else right away, use the functional update form: setCount(prev => prev + 1), and do anything that depends on the result inside a useEffect instead of right after the call.
This usually means someone pushed new commits to that branch after your last pull. Run git pull --rebase origin <branch-name> to bring those in, then push again.

Two common causes: the Flask dev server wasn't restarted after you added the route, or there's a small typo in the route path (like a missing slash). Stop the server, restart it, and double-check the path matches exactly what you're typing in the browser.

faqs.question: How do I resolve a merge conflict in Git?
faqs.answer: Open the conflicting file, look for the <<<<<<< HEAD markers, manually decide which changes to keep, remove the markers, then git add the file and continue the merge or rebase.

faqs.question: Why does my React component re-render twice in development?
faqs.answer: This is expected behavior from React's StrictMode in development — it intentionally double-invokes certain functions to help surface side-effect bugs. It does not happen in production builds.

faqs.question: What's the difference between == and === in JavaScript?
faqs.answer: == compares values after type coercion, while === compares both value and type without coercion. Using === is generally recommended to avoid unexpected bugs.
